files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
### Since 0.16 at a glance

The short version for the app store; the details follow below and under
0.17.0.

- **Runs on PostgreSQL** as well as MySQL and MariaDB, and so also in
  Nextcloud All-in-One.
- **Easier to set up:** a guided setup leads through the first
  configuration one page at a time, and four scenarios in plain words
  (keep an archive, plan concerts, support singers, show the repertoire
  publicly) choose what Cantoria does for your choir.
- **Bring your catalog along:** import from Excel (.xlsx) and OpenDocument
  (.ods) as well as CSV, with a template to fill in.
- **Share a whole programme with the choir** in one step, with a message
  to copy; links can be extended, also up to 30 days after they ended.
- **For the choir members:** "Shared with me" lists the pieces of a
  programme in its order and remembers the chosen voice; one switch keeps
  pieces for practising without a network; the concert folder has a stage
  view that keeps the screen on.
- **To print:** songbooks with cover, contents and page numbers, a
  programme booklet for the audience and large-print parts for singers
  with a visual impairment, each only as far as the rights allow.
- **Finding and planning repertoire:** filters by scoring, language and
  duration, sorting by the last performance, a new programme from an
  existing one, the ranges of the voices with a choir profile, and a pitch
  sheet for a programme.
- **Stricter with rights:** the scan of a public link needs a license for
  its download, and a link ends at the latest when the license that
  releases it ends.

### Added

- **Guided setup.** On a new instance the settings page opens a dialog that
  leads through the first configuration one page at a time: a welcome with
  what is needed, then five steps (archive folder, functions for the choir,
  roles and groups, the access check, import and file sync in the app) and
  an overview with the state of each step. It uses the same forms as the
  page and starts on the first step that is not done. **Continue** saves
  what a page holds; going back or closing with input that is not saved asks
  first. **Set up step by step** opens it again; the empty app links to it
  for administrators.
- **Ranges of the voices and the choir profile** (module "Facts from the
  scores"). The app reads from every MusicXML file the range and tessitura
  of each voice, the first tones, the keys and the first bars, in the
  background and whenever a score is opened. The details of a copy show
  them in the section "Music"; the conductor describes the choir in the
  choir profile (voice groups, never single singers), and the catalog
  filter "Our ranges" finds pieces that fit, with a suggested
  transposition. Migration `Version001800Date20261112120000` adds the
  table `cantoria_score_facts`.
- **Pitch sheet and the programme at a glance.** A concert or song list
  shows its pieces as a band with lengths, keys and a sign for every
  transition, and a pitch sheet with the first tone of every voice per
  piece, to play and to print.
- **Programme booklet** (module "Programme booklet"). A PDF for the
  audience from a concert: cover, programme with the people and their life
  dates, and the lyrics read from the MusicXML with a translation. Lyrics
  are printed only with confirmed public domain or a license for
  publication (`RightsPolicy::bookletLyricsDenial`). New version fields
  "Translation of the lyrics" and "Translator and source of the
  translation".
- **Large-print parts** (module "Large-print parts"). One voice of a score
  set large for a singer with a visual impairment and printed from the
  score view. Needs confirmed public domain, a license (new use
  "Accessible format") or the confirmation of the catalog librarian that
  the part is an accessible copy (§ 45b UrhG); every part is recorded
  without the name of the singer.
- **Sung practice voice.** The playback and the practice files can sound
  like singing: each note takes the vowel of its syllable. A synthetic
  sound made in the browser; vowels only.
- **Annual report as a booklet (PDF)** with the year in large figures and
  the concerts as a timeline.
- **Design** (`docs/design.md`): a colour and letter per voice group in
  the mixer, the ranges and the score; the first bars of a piece in the
  catalog, tasks and programmes; a transport bar with measure, tempo and
  voice buttons for practising; the next concert on the start page;
  drawings for empty views; public pages with the colour and the logo of
  the choir.
- **Guides** in English and German for all of the above, the legal
  background of lyrics in a booklet and of large print (§ 45b UrhG), and
  the new routes in `docs/api.md`.
- **A backup of any size.** The complete backup is sent block by block
  when it is downloaded and read row by row when it is restored, so its
  size no longer depends on the memory of PHP. A restore still checks the
  whole file before it writes anything and writes in one transaction. The
  limit for a restore is 512 MB; `occ cantoria:restore` and
  `occ cantoria:export` work the same way. Tables a backup of a later
  version may bring are skipped, whatever their shape.
- **Home screen.** The concert folder and a public link bring their own
  web app manifest (`/concert-folder/manifest`, `/p/{token}/manifest`), so
  an icon on the home screen opens that page and not the Nextcloud start
  page. The manifest of a link holds no data and answers the same whether
  or not the link exists and public links are on. Not yet checked on real
  devices; the hint about the bookmark in the concert folder stays until
  then.
- **Protection:** confirmed public-domain versions whose proposal now
  reads "unknown" because the arranger is missing come up again under
  "Protection", in a group of their own, and count among the open rights
  on the start page. Links stay as they are.
- **Hand-over folder:** the manifest remembers how a MusicXML file was
  cleaned. When the cleaning changes with a later version, the next run
  writes the old files again.
- **Links that end soon.** The start page has a card for links that end
  within a week or have ended, for everyone who may extend them; the view
  "Links" lists them first and counts them. "Shared with me" says when a
  link ends within a week and who can extend it.
- **Performance import counts as the choir does.** The counting rule can
  be set in the dry run: several participations that count (the own choir
  and joint concerts), the words in the state that exclude a line (now also
  uncertain lines and mere work or song lists), and lines of annual or
  monthly lists no longer count twice when the same work counts in a
  concert with a day date of that year or month. Dates `YYYY-MM` are kept.
  An unclear line that names a composer gets the matching candidate first
  and a note, as a suggestion. The repertoire thresholds can be measured
  from a fixed **reference year** instead of the current year.
- **After the review against the processes of a choir of 6 November 2026
  (import and export):**
  - The columns `Werkgruppe`, `Status`, `Fassung`, `Bezug` and `Gilt für
    den Chor` of the catalog format. Rows of one work group become versions
    of one work, named by the row of the main shelf mark; status and kind of
    version with their German values; the valid version is written by the
    export and read only into an empty catalog, because the conductor sets
    it in the app. Backups in the extended format of 0.17, which name these
    fields `copy.status`, `version.kind` and so on, are still read.
  - A rights status confirmed in the app is not overwritten by an import;
    `lizenziert` is read as protected, with a note to record the license.
  - A preservation copy whose reasoning says "ZU PRÜFEN" starts with the
    original as the working assumption of the board; a protected version
    with MusicXML that is no preservation copy is reported.
  - The import report counts the status of the copies, the work groups and
    the copies that joined their group; exports and snapshots in the
    archive folder say how many internal preservation copies they leave
    out.
  - **Derive contributors from the catalog** (Archive management → Import
    persons): the texts "Komponist" and "Bearbeiter/Text" become persons
    with their roles, life dates and GND number; "Text:", "Satz:",
    "Bearbeitung:", "dt. Text:", "Deutscher Text und Satz:" and the like name
    the roles, "Volkslied" and "Spiritual" mark the melody as traditional. A
    contribution with the role "unspecified" from the person import gets
    its role. A dry run first; the report lists segments without a role
    phrase and persons whose life dates differ from the catalog. A birth
    year without a death ("* 1944") now means living.

### Changed

- **Settings page.** Leaving the page with a chosen but unsaved archive
  folder or unsaved role groups asks first.
- The mixer shows the voice group of each voice; the note with a shared
  piece is a slip beside the notes.
- The version on `main` is 0.18.0-dev.2 for the new table and routes.
- **"Shared with me" with many links** reads the authors of a piece in one
  query and the licenses of a version once per request; a load test with
  200 links counts the queries.
- **One playback** for the score view of the archive and the shared pages
  (`src/score/usePlayback.ts`) instead of two copies, with a test.
- **Docs and store text:** "Cantoria alongside a choir system" (English
  and German) and the store description say how Cantoria differs from the
  Orchestra Scores Manager; `docs/release.md` has a step for the summary
  of the version in the store.
- **After the UX and design review of 16 November 2026:**
  - Concert folder: "End of the programme" stands only under the last
    piece, no longer under every piece with notes. An empty folder leads
    to the concerts.
  - Shared pages: what was removed from the device can be read and not
    only heard; long button labels wrap instead of ending in
    "…"; the bar of the notes wraps on a narrow screen; the chosen voice
    has a tick, not only a colour; the tempo is announced once per change;
    a browser that cannot keep pieces says what usually helps; a public
    link shows until when it is valid, and a page that could not load
    offers to reload.
  - Links: the dialogs to revoke and to extend name the piece; revoking
    says what happens to pieces kept on devices; "Copy link" and "Revoke
    link" have a tooltip.
  - In a low window (up to 560 px high, for example a phone held
    sideways) the header of a view scrolls with the page instead of
    covering it.
  - Sliders for tempo, level and volume have a label with their name
    only; the names of the scenarios in the settings are headings;
    "Protection" says where a shelf mark leads; spacing on the grid.
- **Comparing with the choir system.** A file that is neither CSV nor
  XLSX (an old Excel file, a web page, XML or OpenDocument) is refused with
  what to do instead, not with "no shelf mark". The guide "Cantoria
  alongside a choir system" explains how to prepare the export: a field
  with the shelf mark, CSV, all rows, the whole list and not the plan of one
  date, with Singste as an example.

lines: A tagged pre-release is a release of its own: make changelog writes its section and make tag asks for it. The App Store shows it with the stable 0.18.0.
The App Store shows no changelog on the page of 0.18.0-dev.2.
For a version with a '-' it reads the Unreleased section, which holds 185 lines in CHANGELOG.md. The section of 0.18.0-dev.2 appears with the stable 0.18.0, below that release's own section.
